sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Why a web of trust works now: commodity primitives, an engine the user never sees, links that count both ways.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Earlier failures, commodity primitives, a transparent engine, two-way links, provenance, hard to game.

sections.label: Why now
sections.line: Earlier key stores failed for want of workflows; the February briefs had the ideas; the pieces are now commodity.

sections.label: The primitives
sections.line: A site per person, mature PKI, keys anywhere, git, QR codes, and an agent engine, even a small model.

sections.label: Links only count from the other side
sections.line: Anyone can link to anyone; only returned links count; a page holds only its owner's links.

sections.label: Kinds and provenance
sections.line: Kinds plus date, place and event make links confirmable; agents nudge; checks mostly in code.

sections.label: Schemas each owner defines
sections.line: Each owner defines their schema; only nodes, edges and signatures stay constant.

sections.label: Easy to game one node, hard to game them all
sections.line: Easy to game one node, hard to game them all at once.

sections.label: Identity, in the open
sections.line: Open identity at scale, author-signed content, and every identity provider as evidence.

sections.label: Towards a standard
sections.line: Next: a small standard for keys, links, claims, confirmation and walking the graph.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Kinds and provenance proposed; small models a bet; DNS later.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: My thinking, my February and March briefs, and pki.sgit.ai, on 21 November 2026.
